title: Local App design spec
$comment: PHASE 2 CONTENT, transcription not invention. This schema was drafted as a byte-for-byte transcription of design-result schemas once planned for two SEPARATE builtin workflows (design §18 Phase 4, §8.3 'only one build workflow'), tagged below as DESIGN_RESULT_SCHEMA from `local_app_build_workflow.js` (react_dom / routed branch) and from `local_app_canvas_workflow.js` (canvas_2d|three_3d|phaser_2d|babylon_3d / drawn-surface branch). Neither file exists anywhere in this repo (grepped; zero hits) — the plugin ships ONE unified build workflow instead, `lingxi-code/plugins/lingxi-local-app/workflows/local-app-build.js`, whose actual, much slimmer `designSchema` is `{runtime_family, acceptance_checks, summary}` (required). Those two drafted schemas diverge STRUCTURALLY, not just optionally (compare 'information_architecture' vs 'drawn_surface'/'runtime_family'), and the design doc does not specify how design §18 Phase 4 merges them into one unified schema for the unified build workflow. Rather than invent that merge, this file expresses a discriminated union of the two draft shapes as a design-only reference — not a schema any production code enforces. Whoever implements Phase 4's unification should treat this file as a starting point to edit, not a settled answer. additionalProperties:false is added on each branch (not present in the draft schemas, which are permissive by omission) so oneOf can actually discriminate between the two branches; this is a Phase 2 authoring choice, not something enforced anywhere today.

targets.description: Confirmed native targets as {os, form_factor} entries.

runtime_family.description: The persisted runtime profile family. Preserve it exactly; do not select a different runtime from prompt wording.

drawn_surface.description: Explicitly separates the primary drawn scene from its UI overlays.

hud_overlay.description: HUD/menu/overlay contract, including safe-area placement and phase relation.

loop.description: What advances every frame, in terms of dt: motion, spawning, collision, scoring. Name what is simulated, not how it is drawn.

phases.description: The phase machine, e.g. menu, playing, paused, over. Each entry names the phase and what leaves it.

inputs.description: Every action the player can take, each with BOTH its pointer form and its key form.

end_conditions.description: How a run ends and what carries over between runs.

frame_budget.description: Roughly what has to be drawn per frame and why it fits a phone GPU: entity counts, draw calls, texture sizes.
